abstract: Lichen simplex chronicus (LSC) is a chronic pruritic skin condition, and one of its central features is the itch-scratch cycle. It has been hypothesized that resisting the urge to scratch, and thereby stopping this cycle, may depend on mechanisms of cognitive control. Here, we used the Multi-Source Interference Task (MSIT) during fMRI to examine whether patients with LSC (n = 9) differ from healthy controls (n = 11) in interference control or in the brain activity that supports it. Our results show that both groups had the expected interference effect, with no statistically significant group differences in behavioral performance or in cingulo-frontal-parietal BOLD activity. Whole-brain analysis revealed a greater interference-related decrease in ventromedial prefrontal cortex activity in patients than in controls. These exploratory findings show distinct patterns of brain activity in LSC while preserving interference control, warranting further investigation in larger samples.
